outputs.exact_statement: For every fixed integer $c\ge0$, it is NP-hard to distinguish pairs $(I,B)$ such that $I$ packs into $B$ bins from pairs such that $I$ cannot be packed into $B+c$ bins. Here $B$ is an integer supplied with the instance, the item sizes are rational, and every item size is strictly greater than $1/6$.
A deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that always uses at most $\operatorname{OPT}(I)+C$ bins for some absolute constant $C$ exists if and only if $\mathsf P=\mathsf{NP}$.

For every integer $d\ge1$, there are two finite rooted trees $T^+,T^-$, an integer $L\ge1$, and positive integer quotas $p_1,\ldots,p_L$ with the following properties.*


1.  *All leaves of both trees have depth $L$. Each tree $T^\sigma$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, has a marking $\mathcal M^\sigma$ such that $$\label{eq:tree-separate-marking}
     \begin{aligned}
     |\mathcal M^\sigma\cap V_\ell(T^\sigma)|&\le p_\ell
     &&(1\le\ell\le L),\\
     |\mathcal M^\sigma\cap\pi|&\ge d
     &&\text{for every root-to-leaf path $\pi$ in $T^\sigma$}.
     \end{aligned}$$*


2.  *For any markings $\mathcal A^+$ and $\mathcal A^-$ satisfying the combined bounds $$\label{eq:tree-combined-quota}
     |\mathcal A^+\cap V_\ell(T^+)|+
     |\mathcal A^-\cap V_\ell(T^-)|\le p_\ell
     \qquad(1\le\ell\le L),$$ at least one of the two trees has a root-to-leaf path that is not hit by its marking.*

*The trees, quotas, and separate markings are constructible by a finite deterministic procedure depending only on $d$.

Fix an integer $c\ge0$ and a real constant $\rho>0$. There is a deterministic polynomial-time construction with the following property. Its input is an explicitly listed simple graph $G=(V,E)$, with $V=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $m=|E|\ge1$, and an integer $0\le k\le n$. Its output is an integer $B$ and an explicit list of $5B$ rational item sizes in $(1/6,1)$ such that:*

1.  *if $G$ has a vertex cover of size at most $k$, the items pack into $B$ unit-capacity bins;*

2.  *any packing into at most $B+c$ bins yields a vertex cover of size at most $k+\rho n$.*

*The running-time and output-length bounds are in ordinary binary encoding; their constants may depend on $c$ and $\rho$.

The embedding has the following properties.*

1.  *Every child cell lies inside its parent. Every nonroot cell lies in the first tenth of its root cell. Distinct depth-$\ell$ cells across the two trees have gaps at least $3\lambda_\ell$.*

2.  *The numbers $b_r$ belong to $[1/2,9/16)$, and distinct job cells have gaps at least $g-\Delta$. All the test intervals of one label are pairwise disjoint.*

3.  *For $1\le\ell\le L$, $\Delta\le\lambda_\ell/10$ and $\lambda_1+2\Delta<g$. An interval of length at most $\lambda_\ell+\Delta$ meets at most one depth-$\ell$ cell. If it contains a point of a leaf cell, that depth-$\ell$ cell is the leaf’s ancestor. An interval of length at most $\lambda_1+\Delta$ meets at most one job cell.*


4.  *For $r=(e,j)$, the two independent order bounds are $$\label{eq:coordinate-order}
            H_{r'}-H_r\ge\theta_e+1\quad(r'>r),\qquad
            \theta_f-\theta_e\ge H_{e,R}+1\quad(f>e).$$

Every item size belongs to $(1/6,1)$, so every feasible bin has at most five items. For a five-item tuple, zero total primary score is equivalent to following Table 1. A feasible five-item tuple has nonpositive total primary score; if that score is zero, its total secondary score is nonpositive. If both totals are zero, feasibility is equivalent to $\sum_iw(i)\le0$. The complete item inventory satisfies $\sum_i p(i)=\sum_iq(i)=0$.

In any packing of the constructed instance into at most $B+c$ bins, fewer than $K$ items lie outside five-item table tuples. At each vertex label $v$, at most $3K$ anchors lie outside good tuples. This is a joint bound on its $\mathrm{Z}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ anchors, and therefore applies to any subset of that label’s anchors.
If the input graph has a vertex cover of size at most $k$, the constructed items can be packed into $B$ bins.

For the instance constructed from the complete graph on four vertices with $k=2$, using the parameters in Equation [eq:parameters], both configuration relaxations have value $B$: $$\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP,ind}}=\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathrm{LP}}=B.$$
If the instance of Theorem 6 packs into at most $B+c$ bins, then its input graph has a vertex cover of size at most $k+\rho n$.

For every label $v$ and every point $a$ in one of its half-open test intervals,  $$\label{eq:sound-test-coverage}
 I_v(a)\ge d-6K.$$

Every vertex $v$ satisfies $$\label{eq:sound-side-choice}
 x_v^+\ge d-6K\qquad\text{or}\qquad x_v^-\ge d-6K.$$

Every nonexcluded position $r\in\mathcal R_v$ satisfies  $$\label{eq:sound-long-matches}
 L_{v,r}\ge d-x_v^+-9K.$$
The set $$C=\{v:x_v^+>d/8\}$$ is a vertex cover.

coverage.checked_domain: All endpoint comparisons and counts are decided exactly for each supplied finite rational input. The vectors cover empty input, degenerate intervals, both endpoint boundaries, ties, negative coordinates, future completions, and repeated intervals.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent sorted endpoint ranks determine completion and baseline prefixes; their difference determines active half-open intervals. Finite vectors do not certify the universal real-valued statement or the complete reduction.
